what: Clicking a same-site link fetches only the next body without reloading the document, and the new body slides in from off the right edge over 1.2s cubic-bezier(.74,0,.07,1), covering the old one (the inner part comes along from −24%, creating a parallax). The old body stays where it was being viewed, pushed halfway to −50% and fading to .2, so the dark stage behind shows through — the header and menu sit outside the wrapper and are never interrupted.

options.dur: Advance duration (s), default 1.2 — 0 switches instantly (about .5 for frequent app-like advancing)
options.ease: Curve of type ‹0.74,0,0.07,1›, default is that
options.shift: Distance the old body text is pushed (%), default −50
options.dim: End opacity at which the old text fades, default .2 — stage color is --kf-contrast-bg
options.lag: Where the new body’s inner part (first child) starts (%), default −24 — 0 means no parallax
options.[data-fx-part=page]: Body to swap in (required). The next document must also have the same wrapper and body

from.where: shared.js page transition — original styled-components keyframes (page-enter 100%→0 · MainInner −24%→0 · page-exit 0→−50% · opacity 1→.2, 1.2s cubic-bezier(.74,0,.07,1), wrapper .IsTransitioning 100vh black) and the old section is kept at the position it was viewed at, using scrollY from routeChangeStart

note: Fetches the next body with fetch and runs only over http — opening with file:// usually navigates away. A document has only one transition, so the wrapper attaches to just one. CSS that exists only on the next page is fetched and attached before the transition, but page scripts are hooked by the consumer in fx:page-enter
